# SSH-011: sshd reachable from anywhere takes keys only and bans brute force

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

When the firewall lets anyone reach sshd, password guessing starts within minutes and never stops. With passwords on, one weak password on any account is a root shell away. With keys only the guessing cannot succeed, but it still fills the logs and costs CPU, and a jail (fail2ban sshd or the CrowdSec sshd collection) is the cheap second layer. The verdict joins the listeners, the firewall rules, the effective sshd config and the fail2ban and CrowdSec state.

## Verify by hand

```sh
ss -tlnp | grep sshd; sudo ufw status verbose; sudo sshd -T | grep -Ei '^(passwordauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication|authenticationmethods)'; sudo fail2ban-client status sshd; sudo cscli collections list | grep sshd
```

## How to fix it

Best: allow SSH only on tailscale0 or from one known source and close the public rule. Otherwise turn off PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractiveAuthentication and enable an sshd jail on the real sshd port, or install the crowdsecurity/sshd collection with a firewall bouncer.

## What a fix can break

Closing the public rule cuts off anyone without the private path: prove a login over the tailnet first and keep the current session open while you test.
